misconceptions.trigger: learner describes self-healing as total damage immunity
misconceptions.feedback: Self-healing usually mitigates certain classes of damage. It does not make a structure indestructible or eliminate all failure modes.

misconceptions.description: Ignoring the cost, weight, and manufacturing penalties of healing systems
misconceptions.trigger: learner recommends self-healing materials without discussing complexity
misconceptions.feedback: Healing mechanisms add cost and design constraints. Their value depends on lifecycle benefits relative to those penalties.

misconceptions.description: Thinking repair capability eliminates the need for monitoring or maintenance
misconceptions.trigger: learner assumes self-healing makes inspection unnecessary
misconceptions.feedback: Self-healing can reduce some maintenance burden, but designers still need monitoring, failure criteria, and inspection strategies.
